key_insight: The paper aims to make visual-reasoning feedback more trustworthy by distinguishing corrections grounded in visual evidence from those driven by language priors or response style.
problem_solved: Verifiable rewards evaluate overall task success but provide little guidance about where visual reasoning fails. Teacher-generated token-level corrections offer finer feedback, yet may mix genuine visual evidence with non-visual influences.
method: Use multimodal reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards for task-level supervision.
Apply on-policy self-distillation using dense token-level corrections from a privileged teacher with an evidence-centered visual view.
Target visually attributable corrections; the truncated abstract does not specify the attribution mechanism or experimental results.
impact: This direction could help practitioners train multimodal models that rely more reliably on visual evidence rather than linguistic shortcuts. Demonstrated gains cannot be assessed from the provided excerpt.

paper_title: Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation
paper_authors: Shiao Xie, Siyu Chen, Jianwei Lv, Xiandong Li, Yujin Wang
